summary: Conrad Bursian (1830–1883) was an archaeologist and historian. Educated at Thomasschule zu Leipzig, Leipzig, and Berlin, he held posts at Leipzig, Zurich, Tübingen, Jena, and Munich.
Conrad M. Arensberg (1910–1997) studied at Harvard University from 1928 to 1934 and served on the faculty at Columbia University from circa 1946 to 1979.

Constance E. Kassor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Smith College and Emory University under Jay L. Garfield, John D. Dunne, and Sara L. McClintock, and was a faculty member at Smith College in 2014.
Constance Powell Chin specializes in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree from San Jose State University in 2012.

Constantin Régamey (1907–1982) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. Educated in Warsaw and Paris under Schayer, Turczyński, Przyluski, and Lalou, he held posts at Warsaw, Fribourg, Lausanne, and the Swiss Asia Society.

Corinna May Lhoir works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she studied at Ghent University and the University of Hamburg, where she served as a lecturer and yoga studies program coordinator.

Corneille Jest (1930–2019) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Paris Descartes University and under André Leroi-Gourhan, and was affiliated with the CNRS from circa 1956 to 1996.

Cornelis Jan Kuiken works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Jaap den Hollander for his MA, he completed his PhD in 2002 at the University of Groningen under Timothy Hugh Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) was a religious studies scholar. Educated at Amsterdam's Athenaeum Illustre, the Remonstrant Seminary, and the University of Amsterdam, he held posts at the Remonstrant Seminary, Leiden University, and Edinburgh.
Corrado Pensa specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli, and held a professorship at Sapienza University of Rome in 1971.
Cortland Dahl works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and was mentored by Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.
Courtney Bruntz specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a post at the Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2015 and at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 2026.

Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge, and worked at the University of Cambridge as curator of its South Asia manuscript collection.
Craig Preston specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia, where he was taught by Jeffrey Hopkins and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Cristina Pecchia works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Sapienza University and Vienna under Gnoli, Torella, Pensa, and Steinkellner, and held posts at IKGA and the University of Vienna.

Cristina Scherrer-Schaub (born 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She served as a professor at the University of Lausanne (circa 1999–2013) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 2000–2013).

Csaba Dezső (born 1973) is an Indologist who completed master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University circa 2004.
Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed a D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Eötvös Loránd University.

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held an assistant professorship at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and a post at the University of Munich (attested 2018).
Culadasa (1944–2021) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu and served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha, attested in 2011.
